67.description: On top of one of the buildings near the Odyssey, the player can find a Moon Pipe which leads to a bonus area. In this bonus area, Mario must ride a moving platform over blocks of lava and capture a Lava Bubble to launch himself in lava cannons.

68.name: Flying Over the Lava Islands
68.description: In the area with the "Treasure of the Lava Islands" Power Moon, the player must capture a Lava Bubble and jump into the first lava cannon seen there. Mario must quickly decapture the Lava Bubble in midlaunch and land on a small floating platform where this Power Moon is found.

1.name: New Donk City's Pest Problem
1.description: The player will receive a Multi Moon after defeating Mechawiggler at the New Donk City Hall.

2.name: Drummer on Board!
2.prerequisite: New Donk City's Pest Problem* and talk to Pauline
2.description: The player must talk to Mayor Pauline at the New Donk City Hall Plaza, where she will ask Mario to find four musicians so that they can perform in the New Donk City Festival. The drummer can be found in the New Donk City Hall Plaza, to the right of the City Hall entrance.

3.name: Guitarist on Board!
3.prerequisite: New Donk City's Pest Problem* and talk to Pauline
3.description: The player must talk to Mayor Pauline at the New Donk City Hall Plaza, where she will ask Mario to find four musicians so that they can perform in the New Donk City Festival. The guitarist can be found in the park area near the Main Street Entrance checkpoint.

4.name: Bassist on Board!
4.prerequisite: New Donk City's Pest Problem* and talk to Pauline
4.description: The player must talk to Mayor Pauline at the New Donk City Hall Plaza, where she will ask Mario to find four musicians so that they can perform in the New Donk City Festival. The bassist can be found in the Mayor Pauline Commemorative Park on a distant rooftop to the east of the City Hall.

5.name: Trumpeter on Board!
5.prerequisite: New Donk City's Pest Problem* and talk to Pauline
5.description: The player must talk to Mayor Pauline at the New Donk City Hall Plaza, where she will ask Mario to find four musicians so that they can perform in the New Donk City Festival. The trumpeter can be found on top of a triangular-shaped building across from City Hall.

6.name: Powering Up the Station
6.prerequisite: New Donk City's Pest Problem, Drummer on Board!, Guitarist on Board!, Bassist on Board!, and Trumpeter on Board!
6.description: The player must defeat the two Big Poison Piranha Plants in the New Donk City Power Plant in order to receive this Power Moon.

7.name: A Traditional Festival!
7.prerequisite: New Donk City's Pest Problem, Drummer on Board!, Guitarist on Board!, Bassist on Board!, and Trumpeter on Board!<ref>https://twitter.com/touval_/status/995722752764952576</ref>
7.description: The player will receive a Multi Moon upon talking to Pauline at the New Donk City Festival.

8.name: Inside an Iron Girder
8.description: Along the western side of the city, the player can find a stack of crates blocking the entrance to an iron girder. If the player destroys the crates and enters the iron girder, they can find a Power Moon at the other end.

9.name: Swaying in the Breeze
9.description: Near the Heliport checkpoint, the player can find a Power Moon in the air above a swinging girder.

10.name: Girder Sandwich
10.description: On the eastern side of the city, the player should look for a Power Moon between two girders. To reach it, Mario must wall jump up the girders to obtain the Moon.

11.name: Glittering Above the Pool
11.description: From the New Donk City Hall Rooftop, the player should look for a rooftop pool on a building to the west. To reach it, Mario must perform a long jump from the City Hall Rooftop to land on top of the building with the pool. Finally, the player must bounce off the nearby umbrella to reach the Power Moon high above the pool.

12.name: Dizzying Heights
12.description: The player must climb to the top of the New Donk City Hall, where a Power Moon can be found waiting.

13.name: Secret Girder Tunnel!
13.description: Near the Odyssey, the player can locate a Power Moon hidden inside an iron girder. To access it, Mario must enter the iron girder through an opening on its northern face.

14.name: Who Piled Garbage on This?
14.description: From the Main Street Entrance checkpoint, the player can either bounce off the bouncy platforms or capture a spark pylon and a pole to reach the building rooftops to its west. On top of the roofs, the player must reach the western corner and find a pile of glowing garbage. If the player ground pounds the spot under the garbage, they will receive a Power Moon.

15.name: Hidden in the Scrap
15.description: At the Mayor Pauline Commemorative Park, the player can find a broken piece of the Mechawiggler. If Mario ground pounds this piece, he will receive a Power Moon.

16.name: Left at the Café?
16.description: At the Outdoor Café, the player should reach the lower rooftop (below the rooftop pool) and locate a pile of birds on the building. If the player ground pounds the spot in the center of the birds, they will be rewarded with a secret Power Moon.

17.name: Caught Hopping on a Building!
17.description: At the Rooftop Garden area, the player can find a rabbit hopping around the rooftops. If Mario catches the rabbit, he will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

18.name: How Do They Take Out the Trash?
18.description: From the New Donk City Hall Rooftop, the player should look for a dumpster on top of an iron girder to the east. To reach the dumpster, Mario must long jump from the City Hall Rooftop to the iron girder. Once Mario opens the dumpster (by throwing Cappy at it), he will receive a Power Moon.

19.name: Metro Kingdom Timer Challenge 1
19.description: On the western side of the city, the player can find a scarecrow. Mario must throw Cappy onto the scarecrow, which will temporarily reveal some seesaws and a Power Moon above them. The player must then use the seesaws to collect the Power Moon before it disappears.

20.name: Metro Kingdom Timer Challenge 2
20.description: At the highest point of the New Donk City Hall Rooftop, the player can find a motor scooter and a P Switch . Mario must jump onto the motor scooter and drive onto the P Switch, which will temporarily reveal a checkered-pathway. The player must then drive across the path and collect the key, which will unlock the Keyhole Pedestal containing the Power Moon. Finally, Mario must collect the Power Moon before it disappears.

21.name: City Gardening: Building Planter
21.description: In the park near the Main Street Entrance checkpoint, the player can find three seeds. Mario must take one of these seeds to a flower pot located on top of a building in the south-western corner of the kingdom, to the left of the RC car course. After about 4 minutes, the seed will fully sprout into a flower, which will reward the player with a Power Moon.

22.name: City Gardening: Plaza Planter
22.description: In the park near the Main Street Entrance checkpoint, the player can find three seeds. Mario must take one of these seeds to a flower pot located in the north-eastern corner of this park. After about 4 minutes, the seed will fully sprout into a flower, which will reward the player with a Power Moon.

23.name: City Gardening: Rooftop Planter
23.description: In the park near the Main Street Entrance checkpoint, the player can find three seeds. Mario must take one of these seeds to a flower pot located on top of the building next to the Slots mini-game room. After about 15-20 minutes, the seed will fully sprout into a flower, which will reward the player with a Power Moon.

24.name: How You Doin', Captain Toad?
24.description: At the northern end of the kingdom, the player can find Captain Toad on an iron girder. Talking to him will reward Mario with a Power Moon.

25.name: Free Parking: Rooftop Hop
25.description: In the north-eastern corner of the kingdom (on top of a building), the player can find a parking space built for motor scooters. If Mario can take the motor scooter located at the Main Street Entrance checkpoint to this parking space, he will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

26.name: Bench Friends
26.description: Near the Crazy Cap Shop, the player can find a lonely New Donker sitting on a bench. If Mario sits next to this man, he will give the player a Power Moon.

27.name: Shopping in New Donk City
27.description: The player can purchase a Power Moon from the Crazy Cap Shop for 100 yellow Coins .

28.name: Metro Kingdom Slots
28.description: On the western side of the kingdom, the player can find a building decorated with Tostarena-styled wallpaper. If Mario enters this building, he can play the Slots mini-game. Mario must successfully line up all four Moon icons on the slots to win a Power Moon.

29.name: Jump-Rope Hero
29.description: In the park near the Main Street Entrance checkpoint, the player can find two New Donkers hosting the Jump-Rope mini-game. If Mario can score 30 jumps on this mini-game, he will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

30.name: Jump-Rope Genius
30.description: In the park near the Main Street Entrance checkpoint, the player can find two New Donkers hosting the Jump-Rope mini-game. If Mario can score 100 jumps on this mini-game, he will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

31.name: Remotely Captured Car
31.description: Near the Main Street Entrance checkpoint, the player can find a New Donker playing with an RC car. Mario must capture the New Donker in order to control the RC car, which the player must steer into the cage with the Power Moon in order to collect it.

32.name: RC Car Pro!
32.description: Next to the "Remotely Captured Car" Power Moon, the player can find a building with the RC Car mini-game. If Mario can complete the mini-game race (three laps in under 35 seconds), he will receive a Power Moon.

33.name: Taking Notes: In the Private Room
33.description: On the main street, the player should look for an open building along the left side. Mario must enter this building to find a rainbow-colored treble clef. If the player can collect all the notes from the treble clef before they disappear, Mario will receive a Power Moon.

34.name: City Hall Lost & Found
34.description: In the New Donk City Hall Interior, the player should look for a hidden treasure chest at the top of the area. Mario must throw Cappy at the chest, which will open it and reveal a Power Moon.

35.name: Sewer Treasure
35.prerequisite: New Donk City's Pest Problem, Drummer on Board!, Guitarist on Board!, Bassist on Board!, and Trumpeter on Board!
35.description: In the sewers leading to the Underground Power Plant, the player should look for a hidden ledge along the northern wall, where a Power Moon can be found waiting.

36.name: Celebrating in the Streets!
36.description: During the New Donk City Festival, the player should look for a hidden 8-bit pipe that leads to a secret room containing this Power Moon.

37.name: Pushing Through the Crowd
37.description: At the Outdoor Café, the player must enter the open building on the western side. Inside, Mario can find a lever on the left wall. To activate it, the player must throw Cappy at it. This will temporarily cause a Power Moon to appear at the other end of the room. Mario must collect this Power Moon before it disappears.

38.name: High Over the Crowd
38.description: In the area with the "Pushing Through the Crowd" Power Moon, the player should bounce off the awning over the large door at the end of the area in order to reach a hidden platform high above. From this platform, Mario can swing off the three poles to reach a hidden Power Moon.

39.name: Rewiring the Neighborhood
39.description: West of the New Donk City Hall, the player can find a locked door being guarded by a New Donker. In order to enter this door, the player needs to wear both the Builder outfit and the Construction hat. Once Mario enters this building, he must reach the end of the area and collect the five Moon Shards located here in order to receive a Power Moon.

40.name: Off the Beaten Wire
40.description: In the area with the "Rewiring the Neighborhood" Power Moon, the player should look for a shiny wooden crate hidden on a side building accessible via the first spark pylon. If Mario destroys this shiny crate, he will receive a secret Power Moon.

41.name: Moon Shards Under Siege
41.description: On the main street, the player can find a stationary taxi. If Mario captures the taxi, he can use it to drive off to a secret area filled with Sherms and five Moon Shards. If the player can collect all five Moon Shards in this area, they will receive a Power Moon.

42.name: Sharpshooting Under Siege
42.description: In the area with the "Moon Shards Under Siege" Power Moon, the player should look for a hidden metal box located on an iron girder. If Mario uses a Sherm to shoot and destroy this metal box, he will be rewarded with a hidden Power Moon.

43.name: Inside the Rotating Maze
43.description: In the south-western corner of the kingdom (near the Crazy Cap Shop), the player can find a manhole cover on the street. Mario must capture this manhole cover and move it out of the way in order to reveal a hidden entrance below. Within this area, the player must find and collect five Moon Shards, which will reward Mario with a Power Moon.

44.name: Outside the Rotating Maze
44.description: In the area with the "Inside the Rotating Maze" Power Moon, the player must backflip to the top of the rotating maze and then head to the northern end of the maze. If Mario jumps off the northern end, he can find a hidden platform containing this Power Moon.

45.name: Hanging from a High-Rise
45.description: In the area with the "Pushing Through the Crowd" Power Moon, the player can find a Warp Pipe at the end of the area. Mario must enter this Pipe to reach a hidden building rooftop, where a Mini Rocket can be found waiting. The player must capture this Mini Rocket and use it to reach a hidden area in the clouds. Mario must traverse through this area by swinging on bars in order to receive a Power Moon. Alternatively, the player can use Cappy to reach an opening between the gates surrounding the Power Moon.

46.name: Vaulting up a High-Rise
46.description: In the area with the "Hanging from a High-Rise" Power Moon, the player should look for a bar that moves up and down. Mario must ride this pole up to a hidden pole above and use that one to reach yet another moving pole that goes up and down. Finally, the player must use this moving pole to reach a high secret platform where a Power Moon can be found.

47.name: Bullet Billding
47.description: Near the New Donk City Hall Plaza, the player should look for an alleyway with an open building at the end. Mario should enter this building and then traverse to the end of the area within in order to receive a Power Moon.

48.name: One Man's Trash...
48.description: In the area with the "Bullet Billding" Power Moon, the player must capture a Bullet Bill from the first Bill Blaster and then use it to fly across to a hidden platform with a dumpster. If Mario opens the dumpster (by throwing Cappy at it or by crashing the Bullet Bill into it), he will receive a Power Moon.

49.name: Motor Scooter: Escape!
49.description: Near the New Donk City Hall Plaza, the player should look for a triangular-shaped building with an open doorway. Mario must enter this area and then hop on the motor scooter inside. If the player can ride the motor scooter to the end of the area successfully, they will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

50.name: Big Jump: Escape!
50.description: In the area with the "Motor Scooter: Escape!" Power Moon, the player should ride the motor scooter across the top of some wooden crates along the left side in order to find a hidden Power Moon.

51.name: Secret Path to New Donk City!
51.description: This Power Moon can be found on the Isolated Rooftop in the south-eastern corner of the kingdom. To reach it, the player must travel through a painting located in the Sand Kingdom . The painting can be found on a tall stone pillar where the "On the Lone Pillar" Power Moon is located.

52.name: A Tourist in the Metro Kingdom!
52.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and talk to the tourist in Tostarena Town
52.description: After restoring the Sand Kingdom, the player should locate the Desert Wanderer at the Tostarena Town. Mario must talk to the Tostarenan, who states that he wants to go to the Metro Kingdom . Mario can later talk to him near the entrance of New Donk City, and after talking to him there, he awards Mario with a Power Moon.

53.name: Found with Metro Kingdom Art
53.description: On the triangular-shaped building where the trumpeter was found, the player should look for the Hint Art located on a slightly lower ledge facing the City Hall. The Hint Art shows Poochy next to a glowing spot located at the Water Plaza in the Lake Kingdom . If Mario travels to the Lake Kingdom and ground pounds the spot shown by the Hint Art, he will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

54.name: Bird Traveling in the City
54.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
54.description: This bird holding the Power Moon travels around the east side of the city. Mario can jump off certain buildings, street lights, or taxis in order to catch the bird and reveal the Power Moon.

55.name: Mario Signs His Name
55.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
55.description: Letters of Mario's name are scattered around northern Squawks Park. In order to obtain this Power Moon, Mario must capture each of the letters and insert them into the nearby plinths. When all the letters are aligned in the right order, a Power Moon appears in front of the letters.

56.name: Surprise Clown!
56.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
56.description: At the very northwest corner of New Donk City proper, Mario can find a New Donker. If Mario talks to the New Donker, he says he could really use a laugh. Mario has to show up to him wearing the Clown Suit and Clown Hat to make him laugh. He will then give Mario a Power Moon as a thanks.

57.name: A Request from the Mayor
57.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
57.description: Mario can talk to Mayor Pauline, who will ask him questions about herself so he can learn more about her. After getting four questions in a row right, she tells Mario that it's her birthday today, and would appreciate a gift. Mario must find a new handbag located on a metal platform east of New Donk City Hall. After presenting Pauline the handbag, she gladly gives Mario a Power Moon in return.

58.name: Jammin' in the Metro Kingdom
58.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
58.description: At Southern Squawks Park, Mario can find a Toad listening to music. If Mario talks to the Toad, he will request that the player play a specific piece of music related to the theme of "revving a tiny engine". Only the "RC Car" (#80) music will earn the player a Power Moon.

59.name: Sphynx in the City
59.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
59.description: The player can capture the binoculars in southern Cranky Avenue and look northwest to find the Sphynx sailing across the sky. Upon doing so, the Power Moon will land on east Squawks Park.

60.name: Free Parking: Leap of Faith
60.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
60.description: A New Donker has started another scooter parking service atop the building at the intersection of Cranky Avenue and northern Squawks Park Street. To use his service and obtain the Power Moon, Mario must find the scooter at the top of New Donk City Hall, mount it, then jump all the way down to the eastern buildings to get to the parking space. The parking space is near the Green Koopa Troopa racer who hosts the Koopa Freerunning race for this kingdom.

61.name: Metro Kingdom Regular Cup
61.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
61.description: Atop an eastern building near the "Free Parking: Leap of Faith" Power Moon, the player can find a Koopa Troopa hosting the Koopa Freerunning mini-game. Mario must enter the race and then reach the finish line in first place to be awarded a Power Moon.

62.name: Hat-and-Seek: In the City
62.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
62.description: A Bonneter on the intersection of Cranky Avenue and southern Squawks Park Street says two of his friends wandered off. One of them is in New Donk City proper, riding on the head of a man who walks along the sidewalks of eastern Cranky Avenue and northern Squawks Park Street. Talking to the Bonneter will give Mario this Power Moon.

63.name: Powering Up the Power Plant
63.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
63.description: In the generator room of the Underground Power Plant, there is a large battery that is to be installed to the power plant. The battery can be captured by Mario, and can moved around like the previous puzzle part from the Lake Kingdom. Once the battery is properly installed, the Power Moon appears.

64.name: Up on the Big Screen
64.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
64.description: There is a movie theater on the west side and the north end of Krool Avenue. Inside the projection room, Mario can enter an 8-bit pipe to enter the projection screen, showcasing a remake of World 1-1 of Super Mario Bros. The overworld of the level has five Moon Shards scattered across. Collecting all five shards reveals the Power Moon in the projection room.

65.name: Down Inside the Big Screen
65.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and complete the game
65.description: Within the projection screen of the movie theater, Mario can enter the fourth pipe of the level to find a hidden underground room with several coins and the Power Moon.

66.name: Peach in the Metro Kingdom
66.prerequisite: A Traditional Festival! and talk to the Toad at Peach's Castle
66.description: Peach and Tiara can be found atop the movie theater building on the west side of the city. Peach offers a Power Moon upon talking to them.

67.name: Hanging Between Buildings
67.description: Atop the triangular building alongside Rattley Street, Mario can ground pound the red button to reveal a black and white pathway with a time limit to the other triangular building. The Power Moon floats high above the middle of this pathway, so Mario must use a ground pound jump or a somersault to reach it.

68.name: Crossing Lines
68.description: This moon floats above some coins and an electric wire connected to the theater building and the Rooftop Garden. Mario must capture either spark pylon, ride the wire, then, with the right timing, jump up toward the coins and the Power Moon.

69.name: Out of a Crate in the City
69.description: The Power Moon is inside a crate on top of the northwest apartment building that leads to the crowded alleyway. When Mario breaks the crate, the Power Moon will land on the Banana Bagels sign. Mario must then dive and cap jump off the water tank to reach this Power Moon.

70.name: Bird Traveling in the Park
70.description: This bird only flies around Mayor Pauline Commemorative Park. This bird can be best caught via somersault or ground pound jump as it flies over the eastern benches.

71.name: Metro Kingdom Timer Challenge 3
71.description: There is a scarecrow on the south sidewalk of Dixie Street. When Cappy activates the scarecrow, the Power Moon appears on the square platform in the construction site, with only 10 seconds to grab the moon. Mario can use a motor scooter to reach the Power Moon in time.

72.name: Found in the Park! Good Dog!
72.description: There is a Nintendog on the northeast corner of Mayor Pauline Commemorative Park. Upon befriending the Nintendog, it will dig around certain spots in the park that Mario can ground pound to reveal coins or the Power Moon, in which the moon is buried in the southeast corner of the park.

73.name: RC Car Champ!
73.description: Next to the "Remotely Captured Car" Power Moon, the player can find a building with the RC Car mini-game. This time, Mario must complete the mini-game race (three laps in under 26 seconds) to receive a Power Moon.

74.name: Metro Kingdom Master Cup
74.description: Atop an eastern building near the "Free Parking: Leap of Faith" Power Moon, the player can find a Koopa Troopa hosting the Koopa Freerunning mini-game. Mario must enter the race and then reach the finish line in first place to be awarded a Power Moon.

75.name: Hat-and-Seek: In the Crowd
75.description: In the area with the "Pushing Through The Crowd" Power Moon, the player must wait for a specific New Donker wearing a Bonneter on his head to come out from among the large crowd and must talk to him to receive the Power Moon.

76.name: Scaling Pitchblack Mountain
76.description: Near the area that the handbag for the "A Request from the Mayor" Power Moon is found, the player can find a Moon Pipe which leads to a bonus area. In this bonus area, Mario must climb up a "mountain" of blue platforms in a dark room while avoiding Stairface Ogres and can find the Power Moon at the very top on a column surrounded by spikes.

77.name: Reaching Pitchblack Island
77.description: In the area with the "Scaling Pitchblack Mountain" Power Moon, the player can find a glowing spot located on a small platform separate from the main "mountain". There are Hidden Blocks that Mario can see by throwing Cappy at them, allowing him to safely cross. He must ground pound the glowing spot for the Power Moon to appear.

78.name: Swinging Scaffolding: Jump!
78.description: On top of one of the buildings south of a triangular building with the ground-pound switch , the player can find a Moon Pipe which leads to a bonus area. In this bonus area, Mario must make it through a series of obstacles, including Swinging Scaffoldings with Hammer Bros on them.

79.name: Swinging Scaffolding: Break!
79.description: In the area with the "Swinging Scaffolding: Jump!" Power Moon, Mario should look for an area with a set of breakable blocks on the far left side. To obtain the Power Moon, Mario must capture a Hammer Bro and throw hammers at the blocks to destroy them and reveal the Power Moon.

80.name: Motor Scooter Daredevil!
80.description: On top of one of the buildings near a spark pylon, the player can find a Moon Pipe which leads to a bonus area. In this bonus area, Mario must ride a Motor Scooter across many falling blocks as well as hit multiple P Switches to make temporary platforms appear. Many coin rings and Sherms are found along the way.

81.name: Full-Throttle Scooting!
81.description: Near the end of the area with the "Motor Scooter Daredevil!" Power Moon, Mario must make a sharp right turn onto a series of falling blocks that form a thin staircase-like path. At the end of this path, the player can find the Power Moon.

1.name: Shining Above the Moon
1.description: Next to the Odyssey , Mario can find a crater. Above the crater are three Hidden Blocks with the Power Moon found above the third Hidden Block.

2.name: Along the Cliff Face
2.description: To the far left side of the Odyssey on a lower platform, Mario can find an 8-bit pipe which leads to a 2D area with a few Fuzzies and the Power Moon found at the end.

3.name: The Tip of a White Spire
3.description: On the roof of the Wedding Hall building, Mario can find a glowing spot on one of the thin spires. Mario must throw and spin Cappy onto the glowing spot to make this Power Moon appear.

4.name: Rolling Rock on the Moon
4.description: On one of the large craters on the Moon, Mario can find a rock that he must roll until it breaks to obtain this Power Moon.

5.name: Caught Hopping on the Moon!
5.description: At the southeast side of the kingdom, Mario can find a rabbit that he must catch in order to obtain this Power Moon.

6.name: Cliffside Treasure Chest
6.description: Near the Ringing-Bells Plateau checkpoint, Mario must jump across a gap to the left of it to get to a platform with a treasure chest containing the Power Moon.

7.name: Moon Kingdom Timer Challenge 1
7.description: At the far northeast side of the first area, Mario can find a scarecrow on a lower platform. Mario must throw Cappy onto the scarecrow and quickly collect the Power Moon that appears before the timer runs out.

8.name: Taking Notes: On the Moon's Surface
8.description: To the far right of the Ringing-Bells Plateau checkpoint on a higher platform, Mario can find a rainbow-colored treble clef. Mario must touch it and quickly collect all of the notes that appear before the timer runs out.

9.name: Under the Bowser Statue
9.description: At the beginning of the Underground Moon Caverns, Mario must capture the Bowser Statue on the right. He must move the statue to uncover a hole where the Power Moon can be found.

10.name: In a Hole in the Magma
10.description: Near the spark pylon in the Underground Moon Caverns, Mario can find a hole in the lava that has a key inside of it. Mario must collect the key by capturing a Parabones , after which the Power Moon will be unlocked next to the spark pylon.

11.name: Around the Barrier Wall
11.description: In the area of the Underground Moon Caverns with the Banzai Bills , Mario can find this Power Moon behind the second wall in this part.

12.name: On Top of the Cannon
12.description: In the area of the Underground Moon Caverns with the Banzai Bills, Mario can find this Power Moon by ground pounding the top of the second Banzai Bill Cannon .

13.name: Fly to the Treasure Chest and Back
13.description: At the Banzai Bill area of the Underground Moon Caverns, Mario must capture one of the Banzai Bills and fly back to the beginning of the Underground Moon Caverns to find a treasure chest high above the area's entrance, which contains this Power Moon.

14.name: Up in the Rafters
14.description: At the top of the Wedding Hall building, Mario can find a small hole underneath the bell that Mario can jump into. Upon doing so, Mario will be warped to the inside of the Wedding Hall building, where the Power Moon can be found on the thin rafter in front of him.

15.name: Sneaking Around in the Crater
15.description: Near the Odyssey, Mario can find a moving glowing bump in a large crater. Mario must ground pound the bump to obtain this Power Moon.

16.name: Found on the Moon, Good Dog!
16.description: In front of the Crazy Cap shop, Mario can find a Nintendog wearing a space helmet. Mario must lead it to a corner near a crater with a few broken Moon Rocks. The Nintendog will start digging up a glowing spot and Mario must ground pound it to find this Power Moon.

17.name: Moon Shards on the Moon
17.description: At the Wedding Hall building, Mario must collect five Moon Shards around and on the roof of the building to obtain this Power Moon.

18.name: Moon Quiz: Amazing!
18.description: Around the right side of the Quiet Wall, Mario can find the Sphynx. If Mario can answer five of its questions correctly, he will be rewarded with a Power Moon. The answers are "Rocket Flower", "Sheep", "Moon", "Below the bell", and "Floated by airship sail."

19.name: Thanks, Captain Toad!
19.description: Behind the Odyssey, Mario can find Captain Toad among the residents of the other kingdoms. Once Mario talks to him, he will be rewarded with the Power Moon.

20.name: Shopping in Honeylune Ridge
20.description: Mario can purchase this Power Moon from the Crazy Cap shop for 100 gold coins.

21.name: Walking on the Moon!
21.description: Near a large crater with pieces of Moon Rock and a few Moonsnakes , Mario can find a Koopa Troopa hosting the Koopa Trace-Walking mini-game. Mario must earn 80 or more points in the minigame to obtain the Power Moon.

22.name: Moon Kingdom Regular Cup
22.description: At the Wedding Hall, Mario can find a Koopa Troopa hosting the Koopa Freerunning mini-game. Mario must enter the race and then reach the finish line in first place to be awarded a Power Moon.

23.name: Doctor in the House
23.description: Mario must purchase the Doctor Headwear and the Doctor Outfit from the Crazy Cap shop and talk to a Shiverian who can be found inside the Wedding Hall. After speaking with him, Mario will be rewarded with the Power Moon.

24.name: Sphynx's Hidden Vault
24.description: Around the right side of the Quiet Wall, Mario can find the Sphynx. If Mario can answer one of its questions correctly, the Sphynx will open up a doorway which leads to a room with multiple coin piles and a treasure chest which contains the Power Moon.

25.name: A Tourist in the Moon Kingdom!
25.prerequisite: A Tourist in the Luncheon Kingdom!
25.description: After restoring the Sand Kingdom , the player should locate the Desert Wanderer at the Tostarena Town. Mario must talk to the Tostarenan, who states that he wants to go to the Metro Kingdom . After meeting him there, he will later travel to the Cascade and Luncheon Kingdoms, and after talking to him in both kingdoms, he appears behind the Odyssey at the Moon Kingdom. He then awards Mario with a Power Moon after being talked to.

26.name: Peach in the Moon Kingdom
26.prerequisite: Peach in the Cap Kingdom, Peach in the Cascade Kingdom, Peach in the Sand Kingdom, Peach in the Lake Kingdom, Peach in the Wooded Kingdom, Peach in the Cloud Kingdom, Peach in the Lost Kingdom, Peach in the Metro Kingdom, Peach in the Snow Kingdom, Peach in the Seaside Kingdom, Peach in the Luncheon Kingdom, Peach in the Ruined Kingdom, and Peach in Bowser's Kingdom
26.description: At the top of the Wedding Hall building next to the bell, Mario can find Princess Peach and Tiara . Mario must speak with them, after which they will give him the Power Moon.

27.name: Found with Moon Kingdom Art
27.description: Inside the Wedding Hall on the right wall, Mario can find a piece of Hint Art . The Hint Art shows Poochy on a glowing spot in the corner of a wall next to a scarecrow in the Wooded Kingdom . If Mario travels to the Wooded Kingdom and ground pounds the spot shown by the Hint Art, he will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

28.name: Mysterious Flying Object
28.description: To the right side of the Wedding Hall building near a ledge, Mario can find a glowing UFO-like creature. Mario must throw Cappy at it before it flies away to obtain this Power Moon.

29.name: Hidden on the Side of the Cliff
29.description: This Power Moon can be found floating high above the Sphynx and can be grabbed by either wall jumping up the wall or by falling off the edge near the Ever-After Hill checkpoint.

30.name: Jumping High as a Frog
30.description: At the eastern-most platform in the kingdom, Mario should notice a Power Moon floating high above said platform. To reach it, Mario must capture the frog near the Wedding Hall building and backtrack to said platform. He must then jump while still captured as the frog to obtain this Power Moon.

31.name: Moon Kingdom Timer Challenge 2
31.description: Behind the Ringing-Bells Plateau checkpoint, Mario can find a scarecrow. Mario must throw Cappy onto the scarecrow and collect the Power Moon that appears before the timer runs out.

32.name: Walking on the Moon: Again!
32.description: Near a large crater with pieces of Moon Rock and a few Moonsnakes,Mario can find a Koopa Troopa hosting the Koopa Trace-Walking mini-game. Mario must earn 90 or more points in the minigame to obtain another Power Moon.

33.name: Moon Kingdom Master Cup
33.description: At the Wedding Hall, Mario can find a Koopa Troopa hosting the Koopa Freerunning mini-game. Mario must enter the race and then reach the finish line in first place to be awarded a Power Moon.

34.name: Taking Notes: In Low Gravity
34.description: In the 2D area with the "Along the Cliff Face" Power Moon, Mario can find a rainbow-colored treble clef. Mario must touch it and collect all of the notes that appear before the timer runs out.

35.name: Center of the Galaxy
35.description: On top of the tall cliff near the Odyssey, Mario can find a Moon Pipe which leads to a bonus area. In this bonus area, Mario must make it through a 2D area with planets that have their own gravity and move along a path to find the Power Moon at the end.

36.name: Edge of the Galaxy
36.description: In the area with the "Center of the Galaxy" Power Moon, Mario can find this Power Moon by jumping to a thin platform from the third moving planet. Above this platform are two planets moving in a circle with the Power Moon found in the middle of them.

37.name: Navigating Giant Swings
37.description: On top of the tall cliff near a rabbit to the far left of the Odyssey, Mario can find a Moon Pipe which leads to a bonus area. In this bonus area, Mario must make it through multiple giant blue swings while avoiding Astro-Lanceurs .

38.name: A Swing on Top of a Swing
38.description: In the area with the "Navigating Giant Swings" Power Moon, Mario can find this Power Moon by jumping on the first swing found after the second Astro-Lanceur. Above the aforementioned swing is another swing where the Power Moon is found.

1.name: Battle with the Lord of Lightning!
1.description: After exiting the Odyssey, Mario should make his way up the stairs and pull the sword out of the ground using Cappy. A spark pylon will appear that Mario can capture and ride up to the tall tower. A boss fight with the Ruined Dragon will ensue and will reward Mario with a Multi Moon when defeated.

2.name: In the Ancient Treasure Chest
2.description: To the left of the stairs that lead to the spark pylon, there is a ledge that Mario can hold on to. At the end of the ledge is a treasure chest that contains a Power Moon.

3.name: Roulette Tower: Climbed
3.prerequisite: Battle with the Lord of Lightning!
3.description: A Mini Rocket on the battlefield will lead Mario to a roulette block challenge area. After climbing the tower, Mario is rewarded with a Power Moon.

4.name: Roulette Tower: Stopped
4.prerequisite: Battle with the Lord of Lightning!
4.description: Inside the Roulette Tower in the section to the left of where the red Koopa Troopas are.

5.name: Peach in the Ruined Kingdom
5.prerequisite: Talk to the Toad at Peach's Castle
5.description: Peach and Tiara are on the battlefield, to the right of the dragon.

6.name: Caught on a Big Horn
6.description: Obtained by throwing Cappy onto the dragon's left horn and holding him there until the Power Moon appears.

7.name: Upon the Broken Arch
7.description: On top of the broken arch on the right side of the staircase.

8.name: Rolling Rock on the Battlefield
8.description: On the battlefield, there is a loose rock that must be thrown 50 times or hit another rock near the Ruined Dragon to reveal a Power Moon.

9.name: Charging Through an Army
9.description: Inside a Moon Pipe that appears next to the Odyssey. The pipe leads to an area where Mario must bust open a cage by capturing a Chargin' Chuck .

10.name: The Mummy Army's Curse
10.description: In the area led to by the Moon Pipe; after the Chinchos start appearing, Mario must return to the beginning of the area, where a sparkling Chincho will spawn. Defeating it reveals the Power Moon.

1.name: Atop the Highest Tower
1.description: The player must traverse through the Tostarena Ruins and reach the top of the Round Tower, where this Power Moon is located.

2.name: Moon Shards in the Sand
2.description: From the top of the Round Tower in the Tostarena Ruins, the player should cross the moving platforms ahead in order to reach the Moe-Eye Habitat . Within the habitat, the player should locate and collect five Moon Shards , which will reward Mario with the Power Moon.

3.name: Showdown on the Inverted Pyramid
3.description: The player will receive a Multi Moon after defeating Hariet on top of the Inverted Pyramid.

4.name: The Hole in the Desert
4.description: The player will receive a Multi Moon after defeating Knucklotec in the Deepest Underground.

5.name: Overlooking the Desert Town
5.description: The player can find a Power Moon located on top of a building in the north-western corner of the Tostarena Town .

6.name: Alcove in the Ruins
6.description: The player can find this Power Moon located in a hidden alcove under the 8-bit section near the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint.

7.name: On the Leaning Pillar
7.description: Near the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint, the player should notice a Power Moon located on a stone pillar. To reach it, Mario must capture a Bullet Bill and use it to collect the Power Moon.

8.name: Hidden Room in the Flowing Sands
8.description: Near the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint, the player should look for a very small alcove on the wall in the quicksand. Mario should sink under the sand to enter the alcove, where he will find a hidden Power Moon.

9.name: Secret of the Mural
9.description: The player can find a hidden Power Moon in the 8-bit section on the Tostarena Ruins Round Tower. It is located in a hidden alcove on the left side of the final moving platform.

10.name: Secret of the Inverted Mural
10.description: The player can find a hidden Power Moon in the 8-bit section on the Inverted Pyramid. It is located in a hidden alcove on the exterior portion of the 8-bit section.

11.name: On Top of the Stone Archway
11.description: From the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint, the player should continue through the Ruins until they reach the top of the 8-bit section. From there, the player must capture a Bullet Bill and use it to fly across to the top of the stone archway at the entrance to the Tostarena Ruins.

12.name: From a Crate in the Ruins
12.description: From the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint, the player should continue through the Ruins until they reach the top of the 8-bit section. From there, the player should look for a shiny wooden crate next to the Bill Blaster . If the player destroys the crate, they will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

13.name: On the Lone Pillar
13.description: The player can either capture the Glydon at the top of Tostarena Ruins Round Tower and use it to glide over to an isolated stone pillar between the Inverted Pyramid and the Jaxi Ruins, Long Jump from the spot on the floating Inverted Pyramid where Jaxi is intended to go, or use a Bullet Bill above Alcove in the Ruins to get there.

14.name: On the Statue's Tail
14.description: At the top of the Inverted Pyramid, the player should head to the Jaxi statue in the north-western corner. If the player throws Cappy at the statue's tail and holds him there for a few seconds, Mario will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

15.name: Hang Your Hat on the Fountain
15.description: In the Tostarena Town, Mario must throw and spin Cappy on the town's fountain for a few seconds, which will reveal this Power Moon.

16.name: Where the Birds Gather
16.description: In the Desert Oasis, the player can find a small mound of sand with several birds on it. If the player ground pounds the top of this mound, they will receive a Power Moon.

17.name: Top of a Dune
17.description: From the Tostarena Town, the player should head west and look for the tallest sand dune. The player must then climb up the dune and ground pound the top of it in order to receive this Power Moon.

18.name: Lost in the Luggage
18.description: Near the entrance to the Inverted Pyramid, the player can find a glowing spot on the sand next to some boxes and tires. If the player grounds pounds the glowing spot, they will receive a Power Moon.

19.name: Bullet Bill Breakthrough
19.description: Near the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint, the player should look for a cage containing the Power Moon. To open the cage, Mario must capture a Bullet Bill and use it to fly into the cage, breaking it and allowing the Power Moon inside to be collected.

20.name: Inside a Block Is a Hard Place
20.description: From the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint, the player should head to the ledge below and look for a shiny stone block. If the player captures a Bullet Bill and uses it to break open this block, they will be rewarded with a Power Moon. This sidequest's name is a pun on "between a rock and a hard place."

21.name: Bird Traveling the Desert
21.description: The player must throw Cappy at a large bird that flies around the Sand Kingdom. (It can easily be hit while it is flying in the Desert Oasis.)

22.name: Bird Traveling the Wastes
22.description: The player can either throw Cappy at a large bird that flies around the Jaxi Ruins or catch the bird while riding a Jaxi.

23.name: The Lurker Under the Stone
23.description: At the top of the Inverted Pyramid, the player should notice a Lurker moving around the area. If the player can ground pound it, they will receive a Power Moon.

24.name: The Treasure of Jaxi Ruins
24.description: Near the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint, the player should look for a large sinkhole in the quicksand. Mario should enter this sinkhole to be taken to the Ice Cave. If Mario can make it to the end of the caves, he will find a Warp Pipe that will take him to the Jaxi Ruins, where two treasure chests can be found. Throwing Cappy at the left treasure chest will cause it to open and reward the player with a Power Moon.

25.name: Desert Gardening: Plaza Seed
25.description: In the Tostarena Town, the player should look for a seed next to three flower pots. Mario should pick up the seed and plant it inside one of the flower pots. After about 30 minutes, the seed will fully sprout into a flower, which will reward the player with a Power Moon.

26.name: Desert Gardening: Ruins Seed
26.description: Near the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar checkpoint, the player should look for a seed inside a hidden alcove on the eastern wall. Mario should pick up the seed and plant it inside one of the flower pots in the Tostarena Town. After about 30 minutes, the seed will fully sprout into a flower, which will reward the player with a Power Moon.

27.name: Desert Gardening: Seed on the Cliff
27.description: South of the Moe-Eye Habitat, the player should look for a seed on a low cliff ledge. Mario should pick up the seed and plant it inside one of the flower pots in the Tostarena Town. After about 30 minutes, the seed will fully sprout into a flower, which will reward the player with a Power Moon.

28.name: Sand Kingdom Timer Challenge 1
28.description: In the Tostarena Northwest Reaches, the player should get on top of the building (either by traversing through the building or by using the Spark Pylons scattered through the Sand Kingdom), where they can find a scarecrow. The player must throw Cappy onto the scarecrow, which will temporarily reveal some blocks and a Power Moon above them. The player must then collect the Power Moon before it disappears.

29.name: Sand Kingdom Timer Challenge 2
29.description: In the Moe-Eye Habitat, the player should look for a P Switch on the southern side. The player must press the P Switch, which will reveal a key and a hidden path (that only the Moe-Eyes can see). The player must then collect the key, which will open the nearby lock and reveal a Power Moon. Finally, the player must collect the Power Moon before it disappears.

30.name: Sand Kingdom Timer Challenge 3
30.description: Near the Jaxi Ruins, the player should look for a scarecrow to the east. The player must throw Cappy onto the scarecrow, which will temporarily reveal some blocks and a Power Moon at the end of the blocks' path. The player can either long jump across the blocks to collect the Power Moon before it disappears or ride a Jaxi to collect the Power Moon on time.

31.name: Found in the Sand! Good Dog!
31.description: In front of the Crazy Cap Shop, the player can find a dog, which will lead Mario across a small section of the desert to the side of a sand dune. The dog will then dig up a glowing spot in the sand, which Mario can ground pound in order to reveal a Power Moon.

32.name: Taking Notes: Jump on the Palm
32.description: In the Desert Oasis, the player can find a rainbow-colored treble clef on top of a palm tree. Mario should collect this treble clef, which will temporarily spawn six notes on top of the palm trees. If the player can collect all the notes before they disappear, Mario will receive a Power Moon.

33.name: Herding Sheep in the Dunes
33.description: Near the base of the Inverted Pyramid, the player can find a Tostarenan who has lost three of his sheep. If the player can find all three sheep (located in the surrounding area) and bring them back to the Tostarenan, he will reward Mario with a Power Moon.

34.name: Fishing in the Oasis
34.description: In the Desert Oasis, the player can find a fishing Lakitu . Mario can capture the Lakitu and use it to fish for a big Cheep Cheep in the water, which will reward the player with a Power Moon.

35.name: Love in the Heart of the Desert
35.description: At the Tostarena Ruins Entrance, the player can find four Goombas . Mario should capture one of the Goombas and then use it to make a Goomba Tower . The player can either take the Goomba Tower to the Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar or lure a Bullet Bill into the hat trampoline with the Goombas, where the Goombette can be found. If the player can successfully get the Goomba Tower to Goombette, she will reward Mario with a Power Moon.

36.name: Among the Five Cactuses
36.description: At the central northern end of the Sand Kingdom, the player can find a tall glowing cactus among some short cacti which holds a Power Moon inside. To destroy the cactus, the player must simply hit the tall cactus while riding a Jaxi.

37.name: You're Quite a Catch, Captain Toad!
37.description: In the Desert Oasis, the player can find a fishing Lakitu. Mario can capture the Lakitu and use it to fish out Captain Toad from the sand at the north end of the Oasis. Captain Toad will then reward the player with a Power Moon.

38.name: Jaxi Reunion!
38.description: To the east of the Desert Oasis, the player can find a Jaxi statue facing an empty pedestal. If Mario rides a Jaxi onto the empty pedestal, the Jaxi will reward him with a Power Moon.

39.name: Welcome Back, Jaxi!
39.description: At the top of the Inverted Pyramid, the player can find a Jaxi stand and an empty pedestal on the southern end of the Pyramid. If Mario calls for a Jaxi and rides him onto the empty pedestal, he will reward him with a Power Moon.

40.name: Wandering Cactus
40.description: To the north of the Desert Oasis, the player can find a cactus with some birds on it. If the player captures the cactus, they can move it out of the way to reveal a glowing spot on the sand. Mario must then ground pound the glowing spot to reveal a Power Moon.

41.name: Sand Quiz: Wonderful!
41.description: Behind the Tostarena Ruins, the player can find a Sphynx. If Mario can answer five of its questions correctly, the player will be rewarded with a Power Moon. The answers are "Ring", "30", "ice", "5", and "Sphynx".

42.name: Shopping in Tostarena
42.description: The player can purchase a Power Moon from the Crazy Cap Shop for 100 yellow Coins .

43.name: Employees Only
43.description: On the left side of the Tostarena Town, the player can find a small alcove that they can enter if they crouch into it. This will lead Mario to the back side of the Crazy Cap Shop, where a Power Moon awaits.

44.name: Sand Kingdom Slots
44.description: In the Tostarena Town, the player can find a door leading to a Slots mini-game. If the player can successfully line up all three Moon icons on the slots, they will receive a Power Moon.

45.name: Walking the Desert!
45.description: In the area between the Tostarena Ruins and the Desert Oasis, the player can find a Koopa Troopa hosting the Koopa Trace-Walking mini-game. If the player can score at least 80 points in this mini-game, they will receive a Power Moon.

46.name: Hidden Room in the Inverted Pyramid
46.description: Near the end of the Inverted Pyramid's interior section, the player should notice some stone pillars moving along a conveyor belt. If the player follows the stone pillars into the wall, they will find a hidden room containing a treasure chest which has this Power Moon.

47.name: Underground Treasure Chest
47.description: In the Underground Temple area, the player must capture a Bullet Bill from the first Bill Blaster and use it to fly to the back side of the wall to the right. They must then traverse across the top of the wall to find a hidden treasure chest, which holds a Power Moon inside.

48.name: Goomba Tower Assembly
48.description: In the Underground Temple area, the player must capture a Goomba and use it to make a Goomba Tower that is tall enough in order to reach the Power Moon floating high up in the area.

49.name: Under the Mummy's Curse
49.description: After defeating Knucklotec, the player should notice the smaller hole in the desert. This will take Mario to the arena where Knucklotec was fought. On this arena, several Chinchos will spawn, including one glowing Chincho, which will reward the player with a Power Moon if defeated.

50.name: Ice Cave Treasure
50.description: In the sinkhole north of Tostarena Ruins Sand Pillar, the player should wall jump up the stone pillars near the exit Warp Pipe in order to find a hidden Power Moon.

51.name: Sphynx's Treasure Vault
51.description: Behind the Tostarena Ruins, the player can find a Sphynx. If Mario can answer one of its questions correctly, the player will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

52.name: A Rumble from the Sandy Floor
52.description: Near the "Overlooking the Desert Town" Power Moon, the player can find a Warp Pipe leading to a secret area. In the secret area, the player should feel where the vibrations of their controller are the strongest. If the player ground pounds that spot, they will receive a Power Moon.

53.name: Dancing with New Friends
53.description: In the Tostarena Town, the player can find a locked door being guarded by a Tostarenan. In order to enter this door, the player needs to wear either the Poncho outfit with the Sombrero hat or the Skeleton Suit outfit with any hat. Once Mario enters the room, he needs to stand on the stage in the center of the room and dance with the other Tostarenans, which will reward him with a Power Moon.

54.name: The Invisible Maze
54.description: North of the Moe-Eye Habitat, the player can find a door leading to a secret area. Within the area, the player needs to utilize the Moe-Eyes in order to cross through three rooms of invisible platforms, which will reward Mario with a Power Moon.

55.name: Skull Sign in the Transparent Maze
55.description: In the area with "The Invisible Maze" Power Moon, the player can find a sign with a skull printed on it. If Mario throws Cappy at the sign and holds him there for a few seconds, the player will be rewarded with a hidden Power Moon.

56.name: The Bullet Bill Maze: Break Through!
56.description: In the Tostarena Northwestern Reaches, the player can find a large building that they can enter. Inside, the player needs to capture Bullet Bills in order to reach the end of the path, where a Power Moon awaits.

57.name: The Bullet Bill Maze: Side Path
57.description: In the area with "The Bullet Bill Maze: Break Through!" Power Moon, the player should look for a spiraling side path about halfway through the maze. Mario should capture a Bullet Bill and use it to head through this side path, where a secret Power Moon awaits.

58.name: Jaxi Driver
58.description: From the Jaxi Ruins checkpoint, the player should use a Jaxi to enter the tunnel located in the poisonous water under said checkpoint. If the player can traverse through this secret area with the Jaxi, they will receive a Power Moon. This sidequest's name is a pun on "taxi driver."

59.name: Jaxi Stunt Driving
59.description: In the area with the "Jaxi Driver" Power Moon, the player can find a side path with a rainbow-colored treble clef. If the player can collect all the notes from the treble clef before they disappear, Mario will receive a secret Power Moon.

60.name: Strange Neighborhood
60.description: In the Tostarena Town, the player can find a Mini Rocket on top of a building on the right side. Mario should capture the rocket to be taken to a secret area, where he must cross several rotating buildings without the help of Cappy. If the player can make it to the end of this secret area, they will receive a Power Moon.

61.name: Above a Strange Neighborhood
61.description: In the area with the "Strange Neighborhood" Power Moon, the player can find a set of three blocks, which hide a hidden block above them. If Mario jumps on top of this hidden block, he can reach a secret Power Moon.

62.name: Secret Path to Tostarena!
62.description: This Power Moon can be found on the Southwestern Floating Island in the sky. To reach it, the player must travel through a painting located in a different kingdom: If the player visits the Lake Kingdom before the Wooded Kingdom, then the painting can be found in a small pool of water in the Courtyard of the Lake Kingdom. If the player visits the Wooded Kingdom before the Lake Kingdom, then the painting can be found behind an iron block on the iron wall in the Wooded Kingdom, which can be reached by traversing atop the wall from the Station 8 checkpoint flag.

63.name: Found with Sand Kingdom Art
63.prerequisite: The Hole in the Desert and complete the game
63.description: In the Tostarena Town, the player can find some Hint Art on an eastern building showing a Power Moon hidden in a different kingdom. Mario must then travel to the spot shown in the painting (the Crazy Cap Shop in Bowser's Kingdom) and ground pound the floor tile (outside the shop) located three spaces away from the checkpoint and six spaces away from the shop entrance.

64.name: Jammin' in the Sand Kingdom
64.prerequisite: The Hole in the Desert and complete the game
64.description: On top of the south-eastern building in the Tostarena Town, the player can find a Toad listening to music. If Mario talks to the Jammin' Toad , he will request that the player play a specific piece of music related to the theme of "memories of a tough battle". If the player selects any boss battle theme from the Music List, the Toad will reward Mario with a Power Moon.

65.name: Hat-and-Seek: In the Sand
65.prerequisite: The Hole in the Desert and complete the game
65.description: In the south-western corner of the Tostarena Town, the player can find a Bonneter disguised as a sombrero on top of a Tostarenan's head. If Mario speaks to the Bonneter, he will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

66.name: Sand Kingdom Regular Cup
66.prerequisite: The Hole in the Desert and complete the game
66.description: At the Tostarena Northwest Reaches, the player can find a Koopa Troopa hosting the Koopa Freerunning mini-game. Mario must enter the race and then reach the finish line in first place to be awarded a Power Moon.

67.name: Binding Band Returned
67.prerequisite: The Hole in the Desert and complete the game
67.description: In the Deepest Underground, the player can find a glowing spot on top of the Binding Band. Mario must ground pound this glowing spot to obtain a Power Moon.

68.name: 'Round-the-World Tourist
68.prerequisite: A Tourist in the Mushroom Kingdom!
68.description: After restoring the Sand Kingdom, Mario should locate the Desert Wanderer at the Tostarena Town. Mario must talk to him here, which will start a side-quest that involves talking to him in every kingdom he visits, being the Metro , Cascade , Luncheon , Moon and Mushroom kingdoms. Afterwards, he returns to the Sand Kingdom. Talking to him here will reward Mario with a Power Moon.

69.name: Peach in the Sand Kingdom
69.prerequisite: The Hole in the Desert and talk to the Toad at Peach's Castle
69.description: On top of the Inverted Pyramid, the player can find Princess Peach . Talking to her will reward Mario with a Power Moon.

70.name: Mighty Leap from the Palm Tree!
70.description: This moon is found above the northernmost palm tree within the Desert Oasis grounds. Its height above the tree will require Mario to either use a ground pound jump, back somersault, or side somersault to reach it.

71.name: On the North Pillar
71.description: This moon is located on a tall stone pillar in northern Tostarena. The player must capture a spark pylon on either the Tostarena Northwest Reaches, the Moe-Eye Habitat, or the Inverted Pyramid and travel to said pillar. Mario must then release capture as he's riding the wire to fall towards the pillar and the moon on it.

72.name: Into the Flowing Sands
72.description: This moon lies in the downward sand flow in the west area of Tostarena Ruins. Mario will slip down if he attempts to climb the sand flow, so he must fall from the moving lifts directly above the sand flow to obtain this moon.

73.name: In the Skies Above the Canyon
73.description: To find this moon, Mario must board the moving platform from the Tostarena Ruins Round Tower. Just before the first platform descends, Mario must jump north to grab this moon.

74.name: Island in the Poison Swamp
74.description: This moon lies on the southernmost islet within the poisonous swamp surrounding Jaxi Ruins. The player needs to ride Jaxi across the swamp to obtain it.

75.name: An Invisible Gleam
75.description: This moon can be found in Moe-Eye Habitat, on top of the second pillar. To grab it, Mario must first possess a Moe-Eye and see the gleam from that pillar while possessed. Then, he can make his way to the pillar and ground-pound its center for the moon.

76.name: On the Eastern Pillar
76.description: As the name suggests, this moon is located on the easternmost pillar, sealed in a stone block. Mario must lure a Bullet Bill to the pillars between Tostarena Ruins and Jaxi Ruins, then capture it. On the way to the easternmost pillar, it's highly recommended that the player shakes the Joy-Con to cover more distance before the Bullet Bill explodes prematurely. If the Joy-Con are inside of the controller peripheral, it can still be obtained by jumping over a Bullet Bill and letting it continue towards the pillar before capturing it, slightly shortening the distance needing traveled.

77.name: Caught Hopping in the Desert!
77.description: West of Tostarena Town, not far from where the Moon Rock was destroyed, there are three rabbits. One of the rabbits is holding a Power Moon, whereas the other two rabbits hold either one or eight coins. The rabbits tend to run away in different directions, and the rabbit with the Power Moon will run northwest of its initial gathering spot.

78.name: Poster Cleanup
78.description: Although Mario defeated Bowser and canceled his wedding with Peach, 17 of Bowser's posters have recently been applied on the walls of building in Tostarena Northwest Reaches. Many of these posters are on higher reaches of the walls, and may require Mario to jump off of the nearby sand mound or the spineless cacti to remove them. Once all 17 posters are removed, a nearby Tostarenan will reward Mario with a Power Moon as a thanks.

79.name: Taking Notes: Running Down
79.description: There is a rainbow treble clef in the near southwesternmost corner of Tostarena, found nearby two large cacti. The notes that spawn form a straight line pointing northeast and last only 10 seconds. Given the rather strict time limit, Mario must ride Jaxi to collect all the notes in time and reveal the Power Moon.

80.name: Taking Notes: In the Wall Painting
80.description: On the second level in the 8-bit mural of Tostarena Ruins Round Tower, the rainbow treble clef is on the north facing side of the tower. Mario must simply collect all the notes to reveal the Power Moon.

81.name: Love at the Edge of the Desert
81.description: After capturing a Goomba at the Tostarena Ruins Entrance, Mario must go around the ruins and head northwest. After traversing a considerable distance, Mario finds the Goombette awaiting at the edge of the area, near the Tostarena Northwest Reaches. If Mario faces her as the captured Goomba, he will be given a Power Moon.

82.name: More Walking in the Desert!
82.description: After completing the previous round of Koopa Trace-Walking, Mario can talk to the Koopa Troopa met between the Tostarena Ruins and the Desert Oasis for a second round. This time, Mario has to score at least 90 points for a Power Moon.

83.name: Sand Kingdom Master Cup
83.description: Mario can talk to the Koopa Troopa in the Tostarena Northwest Reaches again for another round of Koopa Freerunning . Finishing first over the other Koopa Troopa runners awards Mario with a Power Moon.

84.name: Where the Transparent Platforms End
84.description: On one of the two knolls rising between the Odyssey and Tostarena Town lies a Moon Pipe that leads Mario into a sub-area, consisting of an enormous corridor. Mario can capture the Moe-Eye at the entrance and enable its shades to reveal a series of invisible platforms leading to the end of the corridor. Soon afterwards, Mario comes across a wide platform that starts moving along the corridor when stepped on. As he travels on the platform, Mario must navigate a transparent maze whose walls may push him off. Once at the end of the corridor, Mario must jump off the moving platform and collect the Power Moon in front of him. A Moon Pipe leading to the exit is in the same area.

85.name: Jump Onto the Transparent Lift
85.description: At the beginning of the previous area, Mario can capture the Moe-Eye and look down towards the chasm and to the right to spot a platform lying close to the wall. The player can reach the platform by falling off a moving ledge. The platform starts moving once mounted, directing Mario straight into a key that triggers a Power Moon near the entrance at the top. The platform will then lift Mario directly by that spot.

86.name: Colossal Ruins: Dash! Jump!
86.description: Once Mario enters the Moon Pipe at the Tostarena Ruins Entrance, he is brought into a dark area bottomed by a poison lake. Here, Mario must capture a spark pylon to reach a rounding road that immediately starts collapsing in the poison. Mario must evade the sinking road by using several Rocket Flowers . On his way, he eventually has to dash on a huge curving wall, jumping over gaps in the road all the while. After a final stretch, Mario encounters a Power Moon and a long platform rises from the poison, leading him back to the start of the area. Even in Assist Mode, the poison instantly kills Mario if he falls into it.

87.name: Sinking Colossal Ruins: Hurry!
87.description: In the same area as above, Mario can collect a key located near the bottom of the inclined wall. It can be reached by sticking to the lower path, hopping several gaps meanwhile. The key unlocks a Power Moon right beside the starting point, where Mario eventually goes back.

88.name: Through the Freezing Waterway
88.description: At the north-eastern edge of the desert, east from the Inverted Pyramid, is a Moon Pipe located among several cacti and shrubs. It leads Mario to a side-scrolling section, where he has to navigate a channel with long stretches of freezing water. To do so, he must capture Gushens that keep him safe from the water, then charge forward, up and over incoming obstacles, mostly including pools of poison and moving platforms. The water in the channel allows Mario to regenerate the Gushen's water reserve. At the end of the channel, after a long stretch of poison, lie the Power Moon and the exit.

89.name: Freezing Waterway: Hidden Room
89.description: With a Gushen captured, Mario must use the first moving platform to fly further upward, then head to the left and dash through a long poison tunnel. At the end lies a Power Moon, accompanied by some freezing water and another Gushen to help Mario head back.

1.name: The Stone Pillar Seal
1.description: This Power Moon can be found on top of a grassy platform in the middle of the area and can be reached by capturing a Gushen and floating up to it. Collecting it unplugs the first seal.

2.name: The Lighthouse Seal
2.description: Mario must make it to the top of the Lighthouse in order to obtain this Power Moon. Collecting it unplugs the second seal.

3.name: The Hot Spring Seal
3.description: At the Hot Spring Island, Mario must capture a Gushen and spray the lava to make a safe path for him to collect the Power Moon, which is found underwater in the hot spring. Collecting it unplugs the third seal.

4.name: The Seal Above the Canyon
4.description: Mario must make it through the Rolling Canyon area with the shells and past the wall of crates to find this Power Moon. Collecting it unplugs the fourth and final seal.

5.name: The Glass Is Half Full!
5.prerequisite: The Stone Pillar Seal, The Lighthouse Seal, The Hot Spring Seal, and The Seal Above the Canyon
5.description: Mario must defeat Mollusque-Lanceur , after which he will be rewarded with a Multi Moon .

6.name: On the Cliff Overlooking the Beach
6.description: To the right of the Odyssey near the two Goombas wearing pirate hats, the player can find this Power Moon on a high cliff. Mario must capture a Gushen in order to obtain it.

7.name: Ride the Jetstream
7.description: The player can find a hidden alcove to the right of the Odyssey near the Binoculars . Mario must capture a Gushen and float up into the alcove and then right to find this Power Moon above a shallow pool of water.

8.name: Ocean-Bottom Maze: Treasure
8.description: Near the Glass Palace checkpoint, the player can find a set of four 8-bit pipes which all lead to a 2D area flat on the underwater floor. Mario must make it successfully through this 2D area to obtain the Power Moon.

9.name: Ocean-Bottom Maze: Hidden Room
9.description: In the same 2D area as the "Ocean-Bottom Maze: Treasure" Power Moon, Mario must enter the bottom right 8-bit pipe. When he enters the section, he must kick a Koopa Troopa shell into a Brick Block that is blocking the entrance to a hidden alcove containing the Power Moon.

10.name: Underwater Highway Tunnel
10.description: To the northwest of the Lighthouse checkpoint, the player can find three Cheep Cheeps swimming in front of a short tunnel. The player can capture one of the Cheep Cheeps and find a small hole covered by Brick Blocks. Mario must break through these blocks to find the Power Moon hidden inside the hole.

11.name: Shh! It's a Shortcut!
11.description: Near the Ocean Trench East checkpoint, the player must capture a Cheep Cheep and then go a little to the left to find a hole with a path leading to the Power Moon inside.

12.name: Gap in the Ocean Trench
12.description: Near the Ocean Trench East checkpoint, the player must capture a Cheep Cheep and swim forward and down to see the Sphynx . A hole can be found on the right side wall near the Sphynx which leads to a path with the Power Moon at the end.

13.name: Slip Through the Nesting Spot
13.description: Near the Hot Spring Island checkpoint, the player must capture a Cheep Cheep and find a hole to the northeastern side of the area. Mario must avoid the Maw-Rays inside the hole to obtain this Power Moon.

14.name: Merci, Dorrie!
14.description: The player can find this Power Moon floating underneath the purple Dorrie that swims around the area.

15.name: Bonjour, Dorrie!
15.description: The player can find this Power Moon floating high above the yellow Dorrie that swims around the area. It can be obtained by capturing Glydon on the Lighthouse and flying into it or by capturing a Gushen and floating into it.

16.name: Under a Dangerous Ceiling
16.description: Near the Ocean Trench East checkpoint, the player can find this Power Moon by ground pounding a glowing spot on a mound found among many Komboos walking on the ceiling above.

17.name: What the Waves Left Behind
17.description: Near the Rolling Canyon checkpoint, the player can find this Power Moon in a circular hole among the gray rock path. Mario must defeat the Komboo protecting it and ground pound the spot to obtain it.

18.name: The Back Canyon: Excavate!
18.description: On the left side of the Rolling Canyon checkpoint, the player can find this Power Moon by going on a few grassy platforms to find it hidden on a glowing spot with a Moonsnake rolling in its path. Mario must ground pound the glowing spot to obtain the Power Moon.

19.name: Bubblaine Northern Reaches
19.description: Near the Ocean Trench East checkpoint, the player can find three small mounds along with a larger mound in the middle of the three. Mario must ground pound each mound which each has a glowing spot and then ground pound the large middle mound to obtain this Power Moon. Each time Mario pounds the mounds, a group of Komboos will appear.

20.name: Wriggling on the Sandy Bottom
20.description: Near the Lighthouse, the player can find two Cheep Cheeps swimming. Under them is a hidden door which leads to a bonus area. In this bonus area, Mario must ground pound the Lurker to obtain the Power Moon.

21.name: Glass Palace Treasure Chest
21.description: The player can find this Power Moon underneath the Glass Palace in a treasure chest near three swimming Cheep Cheeps and a group of Komboos.

22.name: Treasure Trap Hidden in the Inlet
22.description: Near the Beach House checkpoint, the player can find a small hole underneath the water in a river to the left of the checkpoint. Inside is an area with four treasure chests. Mario must open each treasure chest in the correct order to obtain this Power Moon. The order of the treasure chests is the same order that was used to get the Treasure in the Ocean Cave Power Star in Super Mario 64 's Jolly Roger Bay .

23.name: Sea Gardening: Inlet Seed
23.description: In the small river to the right of the Beach House checkpoint, the player can find a seed sitting underwater on the ground. Mario must pick up the seed and bring it to one of the flower pots on the roof of the Beach House. He must wait for the Power Moon to sprout from a vine, or use a Gushen's water attack to accelerate the growth process.

24.name: Sea Gardening: Canyon Seed
24.description: At the end of the area near "The Back Canyon: Excavate!" Power Moon, the player can find a seed. Mario must pick up the seed and bring it to one of the flower pots on the roof of the Beach House. He must wait for the Power Moon to sprout from a vine, or use a Gushen's water attack to accelerate the growth process.

25.name: Sea Gardening: Hot-Spring Seed
25.description: Near the Hot Spring Island checkpoint, the player can find a seed sitting on a rocky platform along with a Gushen. Mario must pick up the seed and bring it to one of the flower pots on the roof of the Beach House. He must wait for the Power Moon to sprout from a vine, or use a Gushen's water attack to accelerate the growth process.

26.name: Sea Gardening: Ocean Trench Seed
26.description: Near the Ocean Trench East checkpoint and sitting next to the Sphynx, the player can find a seed sitting underwater. Mario must pick up the seed and bring it to one of the flower pots on the roof of the Beach House. He must wait for the Power Moon to sprout from a vine, or use a Gushen's water attack to accelerate the growth process.

27.name: Seaside Kingdom Timer Challenge 1
27.description: Near the Hot Spring Island checkpoint, the player can find a hole underwater containing a ground-pound switch . Mario must hit the switch and then quickly make it through a short 2D area to obtain the Power Moon before the switch's effect wears off.

28.name: Seaside Kingdom Timer Challenge 2
28.description: Near the Glass Palace, the player can find a scarecrow underwater. Mario must throw Cappy onto the scarecrow and then quickly swim over to the Power Moon before the timer runs out.

29.name: Found on the Beach! Good Dog!
29.description: Near the Odyssey, the player can find a Nintendog wearing a fedora. Mario must guide the Nintendog around the area with the binoculars to find a glowing spot near the gray rocks. The Nintendog will start trying to dig it up, but Mario must ground pound the spot to obtain the Power Moon.

30.name: Moon Shards in the Sea
30.description: Near the Rolling Canyon checkpoint, the player can find a scarecrow underwater. Throwing Cappy onto the scarecrow opens up a gate leading to a hidden underwater area. Mario must collect all five Moon Shards in the area while avoiding Maw-Rays to obtain this Power Moon.

31.name: Taking Notes: Ocean Surface Dash
31.description: Near the Beach House checkpoint, the player can find a rainbow-colored treble clef. Mario must throw Cappy at the Rocket Flower next to it and run across the water and collect the line of notes to obtain this Power Moon. A Gushen can also be used to complete this.

32.name: Love by the Seaside
32.description: Mario must capture and create a Goomba Tower and meet with Goombette , who can be found on a platform in the Rolling Canyon path with the shells. She will reward Mario with the Power Moon when he meets her.

33.name: Lighthouse Leaper
33.description: Mario must go to the top of the Lighthouse and capture Glydon. He must fly over to a Bubblainian who is found near the Glass Palace. Upon doing so, the Bubblainian will be impressed by Mario's flying abilities and will reward him with the Power Moon.

34.name: Good Job, Captain Toad!
34.description: Mario must capture a Gushen and take it to the end of the Rolling Canyon path. Mario can find Captain Toad on a higher platform near "The Seal Above the Canyon" Power Moon, who will reward Mario with the Power Moon when he speaks to him.

35.name: Ocean Quiz: Good!
35.description: Near the Ocean Trench East checkpoint, the player can find the Sphynx in the deep area to the southwest of the checkpoint. If Mario can answer five of its questions correctly, the player will be rewarded with a Power Moon. The answers are "Bubblaine", "Four", "Attack", "Resort Outfit", and "To ask questions".

36.name: Shopping in Bubblaine
36.description: The player can purchase this Power Moon from the yellow Crazy Cap shop for 100 gold coins.

37.name: Beach Volleyball: Champ
37.description: In the Beach Volleyball minigame, Mario must hit the ball back and forth 15 times in a row to obtain this Power Moon.

38.name: Beach Volleyball: Hero of the Beach!
38.description: In the Beach Volleyball minigame, Mario must hit the ball back and forth 100 times in a row to obtain this Power Moon.

39.name: Looking Back in the Dark Waterway
39.description: The player can find a hole with a few coin rings which leads to the Underwater Tunnel to the Lighthouse . In the first part with the three swimming Cheep Cheeps, Mario can find this Power Moon inside a small hole in the wall to the left side.

40.name: The Sphynx's Underwater Vault
40.description: Near the Ocean Trench East checkpoint, the player can find the Sphynx in the deep area to the southwest of the checkpoint. If Mario can answer one of its questions correctly, the Sphynx will open up a doorway which leads to an underwater area with a treasure chest containing the Power Moon.

41.name: A Rumble on the Seaside Floor
41.description: Near the Odyssey, the player can find a Warp Pipe on the wall which takes Mario to a room. Inside this room, Mario must ground pound a certain part of the floor to obtain this Power Moon. It can be found more easily if the player has the rumble effect on their controller activated.

42.name: A Relaxing Dance
42.description: The player must purchase the Resort Hat and Resort Outfit or the Sunshine Shades and Sunshine Outfit from the purple Crazy Cap shop and then talk to a Bubblainian who will unlock a door to the Beach House. Inside, Mario must dance with two other Bubblainians for a few seconds, after which Mario will be rewarded with a Power Moon.

43.name: Wading in the Cloud Sea
